meta.source: Coded from the published QP and mark scheme (4MA1_2H_2506, sat 5 June 2025). Derived metadata only. No exam question text transcribed.

coding_notes: CROSSOVER BLOCK CONFIRMED: 2F q18-q28 = 2H q1-q11, a contiguous block of eleven questions worth 40 marks — the same 40-mark overlap as Paper 1. Coded in the same sitting as IGCSE-JUN25-F-P2; the shared rows carry identical tags by construction.

GAP-CANDIDATE differentiation — q17(a), 2 marks, 'find dy/dx' for a cubic. UNTAGGED: unlike the arithmetic series, calculus has NO node in data/skills.ts that covers any part of this, so there is nothing to tag honestly. topic set to algebra so the marks still land in the right column. See docs/audit/25-igcse-4ma1-delta.md section 2.1.

GAP-CANDIDATE stationary_points — q17(b), 4 marks, coordinates of the turning points. Tagged solving_quadratic_equations_factorising as an INTERIM measure: the mark scheme spends most of its marks solving the 3-term quadratic that dy/dx = 0 produces, and a correct answer does demonstrate that. The uncovered part is knowing to differentiate and set to zero.

GAP-CANDIDATE counting_elements_in_sets — q20(b) ONLY, 1 mark, evaluating n(T' intersect C). The CARDINALITY form of set work (spec Higher 1.5 C), which the coded papers show is Higher-only: n() appears on none of the four coded Foundation papers. Tagged venn_diagrams as an INTERIM measure, which over-credits here — venn_diagrams costs 4 and all four are probability skills, and this part involves no probability at all. q20(a) and q20(c) stay genuinely venn_diagrams: completing the diagram and reading a conditional probability off it. One question, three parts, three different tags — which is what makes the split operable.

q21 uses the surface area of a CUBOID, which docs/coding-a-paper.md already records as a standing taxonomy gap (spheres, cones and cylinders each have a node; cuboids do not). Tagged volume_of_a_prism, which covers the volume half the question also needs. Not counted as a new iGCSE gap candidate — it is a pre-existing GCSE one.

q13 is cumulative frequency across four parts: table, graph, median, and a reading above a value. Only (b) is flagged visual — (c) and (d) are read off the student's own graph but restate fine in words.
q22 tagged upper_and_lower_bounds: this is the HIGHER form of the skill, 'solve problems using bounds' (spec 1.8 A), against the Foundation 'identify bounds' form seen on 1F q19.
